vocabulary.codesNote: Cross-checked as a SET against REASON_CODES in src/outcomes.ts by the loader — a code in one place and not the other is a defect, not a widening. `OTHER` is NOT a member: it is declared by the shape ([SD §2.4] rule 3) and the loader refuses it here, which is what lets the Reason union make `remark` mandatory for it alone. Each entry declares its default scope, whether `attribution.party` must name a party, whether a remedy is required and which shape, its disclosure marker and its evidence. [SD §2.6]'s three worked literals are NOT members and could not be: CONSIGNEE_ABSENT bakes a role into the code ([SD §2.4] rule 6 forbids it), REFUSED_DAMAGE encodes an outcome in a verb (rule 1) and SHORT is GOODS_MISSING under another name. See [A4 §4] and the illustrativeOnly block below.
vocabulary.publishedBy: A4 — [A4 §3]. [SD §2.4] fixed the shape and left the list to this area: 'the list itself is A4's job'. Rule 2 bounds its magnitude and is explicitly not a quota; the count is REASON_CODES.length and is deliberately not written here ([A1 §9]).
vocabulary.whenA8Lands: attribution.roleClass is still owed to [A8 §9 item 2] and `partyRequired` below is deliberately a boolean rather than a default roleClass, so that nothing here has to name a member of an enum that does not exist. FORCE_MAJEURE and CAUSE_UNKNOWN need an explicit non-party member of that enum before they can be recorded at all — A4's one concrete requirement on A8.

shape.note: [SD §2.4]'s record, field for field. Five of the six rules below are sourced; two ELEMENTS of this record are authored, and each says so.

ACT | GOODS | PARTY | RESOURCE | SITE | ADMINISTRATIVE
fields.citation: [SD §2.4] — 'it exists so a consumer can separate "something is wrong with the goods" from "something is wrong with the site" without reading a code list, and because HHG's authoring gap is concentrated in SITE and ADMINISTRATIVE'
[SD §2.4] rule 6 — lifting attribution out of the code into its own field

fields.from: SubjectRef[] at portion or item grain
fields.citation: [SD §2.4]; the field that carries [SD §3.4]'s required form for 'delivered, two items short'

fields.from: typed per code — `newWindow` is the one shape a source states and [A4 §3] makes it required on PARTY_ABSENT and PARTY_RESCHEDULED; every other shape is owed to A5

forbiddenFields.why: A reason is NOT keyed by outcome. Rule 1: 'the catalog MUST NOT mint DELIVERED_SHORT and REFUSED_SHORT as two codes.' A reason that named its outcome would be the combinatorial explosion the factorisation exists to prevent, and it would re-create A-TYPE's defect one field to the right.

Rule 4: 'Reason.code does not change when the subject changes grain.' Shippeo republishes 19 of the same (situation, justification) pairs at handling-unit grain under HANDLING_UNIT_* names, and the pair is the same pair.

factorisation.note: THE SETTLED PART. Two axes and only two: the outcome says where in the lifecycle you got to and with what result; the reason says why. The human-readable event name is an ALIAS FOR THE PAIR, never a third axis.
factorisation.aliasRule: A name like ORDER_NOT_DELIVERED_ABSENT is an alias for (situation, justification) and must never be the identity.
factorisation.aliasEvidence: The source is a defect report: Shippeo's SharedEventsOrderConformityOrderNotLoadedPartiallyMissing declares event: 'ORDER_NOT_LOADED_ENTIRELY_MISSING' — the ENTIRELY-missing name on the PARTIALLY-missing schema — while the code pair (ENE/MQP vs ENE/MQT) stays correct in both schemas.
factorisation.citation: [SD §2.1], [SD §2.5] — src:shippeo supplies the factorisation and the grid; src:open-trip-model supplies the enum, the invariant and the sub-results

reuse.rule: Reasons are ORTHOGONAL to outcomes and are reused across them. One reason code appears under several outcomes, and that is the point.
reuse.sourceEvidence: src:shippeo's MQP ('partially missing package') appears under four situations: ECH/MQP (loaded anyway, short), ENE/MQP (not loaded because short), LIV/MQP (DELIVERED anyway, short), REN/MQP (REFUSED because short). Four operationally different things, one reason code, no combinatorial explosion. Shippeo's own analysis calls REN/MQP vs LIV/MQP 'the most important single import' for HHG.
reuse.sourceEvidenceNote: MQP, ECH, ENE, LIV and REN are SHIPPEO's codes, quoted as the evidence for the rule. They are not members of our vocabulary and must not be read as a starting list — ours is `vocabulary.codes` above, published by [A4 §3]. The mapping from Shippeo's codes to ours is in [A4 §3]'s evidence table; MQP and MQT deliberately collapse into one member ([A4 §4.1]).

expectedMagnitude.note: Rule 2's arithmetic, with the measured number rather than the inherited one: ~20 reasons x 5 outcomes, not ~100 types.
expectedMagnitude.measuredFrom: src:shippeo's committed event-list-order-level.md: 40 lines, one header, one separator. Every document's inherited '41 rows / ~20 across 9' is corrected at [SD §2.1] and [SD §5.2 M3].
expectedMagnitude.isATargetNote: A magnitude, not a quota. It bounds what a sane vocabulary looks like; it does not tell A4 how many codes to mint.

openMember.note: The one member the shape itself declares, and the reason src/outcomes.ts keeps it out of the reasonCode() constructor: it carries an obligation the others do not, and the Reason union makes remark MANDATORY for it alone. An OTHER without a narrative is the record both sources forbid.
openMember.citation: [SD §2.4] rule 3 — two independent sources, one regulation-grade: OTM 5.7's 'other' + remark ('the specific reason is provided in the remark property'); src:dp3-400ng Item 226/226A, a Miscellaneous charge for anything without a designated service code, with a MANDATORY detailed note

scopes.citation: [SD §2.4] — one of the two members carrying HHG's authoring gap: shuttle required, long carry, elevator unavailable, parking permit. None of which src:shippeo has.
[SD §2.4] — the other: COI not on file, and its neighbours

scopesNote: The whole six-member enum is [ORIGINAL]. No source publishes it; it exists so a consumer can tell 'something is wrong with the goods' from 'something is wrong with the site' without reading a code list. The loader checks this list against REASON_SCOPES in src/outcomes.ts as a SET — a scope added in one place and not the other is a defect, not a widening.

outcomes.means: The act was performed over its whole intended scope and nothing is wrong.
outcomes.provenance: OTM 'succeeded'; src:shippeo LIV/CFM, ECH/CFM. [ORIGINAL]: collapsing CFM into COMPLETED and FORBIDDING a reason there — a normalisation that also removes Shippeo's DIV overload, glossed three different ways depending on situation.

outcomes.means: Whole scope performed; something about the goods or the circumstances is wrong and is recorded.
outcomes.firstClassNote: THE SETTLED POINT: 'completed with exception' is a FIRST-CLASS OUTCOME, not COMPLETED plus a footnote. src:shippeo is the only source in the corpus that models it that way — LIV carries MQP, RCA and DIV alongside CFM.
outcomes.provenance: The DISTINCTION is Shippeo's — LIV/RCA, delivered-with-damage-accepted, sits under the COMPLETED situation. [ORIGINAL]: rendering it as its own outcome member rather than COMPLETED + a reason.

outcomes.means: The act was performed over LESS THAN its intended scope.
outcomes.firstClassNote: Distinct from COMPLETED_WITH_EXCEPTION by SCOPE OF PERFORMANCE, and that difference is a billing and claims difference, not a shade of meaning. It is why the enum has five members rather than OTM's four.
outcomes.provenance: The distinction is Shippeo's — LIV/MQP (delivered but short) vs LIV/RCA; OTM's partiallySucceeded names it directly. The placement on the outcome axis is ours.
OTM 'failed'; src:shippeo REN (13 rows) and ENE (5).
OTM 'cancelled'. Shippeo has no situation-axis analogue (CANCEL_ORDER is order-level).

attribution.note: Rule 6. Attribution is a structured field ON THE REASON — not baked into the code, and not on the assertion. This SUPERSEDES [fork-time §(b)(7)] ('attribution belongs on the assertion'), which the critique identified as a placement rule no source states.
attribution.roleClassOwedTo: [A8 §9 item 2] — the role enum this would be cut from is undefined. [SD §2.6]'s worked example uses customer, carrier and unknown; three examples are not a vocabulary.
attribution.partyOptionalWhy: Optional BY DEFAULT, refined per code: `vocabulary.codes[].partyRequired` is true for every PARTY-scope member, because a party-side reason that cannot name the party is the DIV overload invariant 2 exists to remove. The responsible party is often unknown when the reason is recorded, which is why the default is optional; roleClass is NOT optional.
attribution.sourcedPart: That reason vocabularies are ORGANISED BY RESPONSIBLE PARTY is sourced: src:stedi-x12-reference element 1651's 86 values are organised that way (consignee-, driver-, shipper-, other-carrier-related) and include 'BF Carrier Keying Error'; src:shippeo separates NJU 'not justified by carrier' from DIV 'by the counterparty'.
attribution.authoredPart: [ORIGINAL]: lifting attribution out of the code into its own field. It removes the duplication both sources carry — Shippeo's REFUSED_LOAD / LOADING_REFUSED_BY_SHIPPER_VARIOUS_REASON are ONE reason with two attributions.

remedy.note: THE SETTLED POINT: a reason may carry its own remedy, and FOR SOME CODES MUST.
remedy.owedTo: A5 — a remedy that opens a storage-in-transit stay, which PARTY_NOT_READY wants. A4 typed the one shape a source states (newWindow) and carries the rest as owed rather than inventing shapes to make the union look finished ([SD §0]).
remedy.sourcedPart: src:shippeo's new_slot {start, end} is REQUIRED on appointment events (OrderAppointmentEvent, SharedTrackingSlot): 'a failed delivery that does not say when it will be retried is an incomplete record.'

rules.statement: Reasons are orthogonal to outcomes and are reused across them. The catalog MUST NOT mint DELIVERED_SHORT and REFUSED_SHORT as two codes.
rules.citation: [SD §2.4] rule 1 — src:shippeo's MQP under four situations
[SD §2.4] rule 2 — Shippeo's 38 published rows from 18 justification codes; the measured factor is 18, not 'twenty-odd', and the argument is the same argument at 18

rules.statement: An open member with a mandatory narrative.
rules.citation: [SD §2.4] rule 3 — two independent sources, one regulation-grade (OTM 5.7; src:dp3-400ng Item 226A)

rules.statement: The same vocabulary at every grain. Reason.code does not change when the subject changes grain.
rules.citation: [SD §2.4] rule 4 — Shippeo republishes 19 of the same pairs at handling-unit grain: HANDLING_UNIT_NOT_DELIVERED_ABSENT IS REN/DAF, exactly as ORDER_NOT_DELIVERED_ABSENT is

rules.statement: A reason may carry its own remedy, and for some codes must.
Attribution is a structured field on the reason, not baked into the code and not on the assertion.
rules.citation: [SD §2.4] rule 6 — the need is sourced three ways; lifting attribution off the code is authored

illustrativeOnly.note: NOT A VOCABULARY, and [A4 §4] found that none of the three could have become one. These are the literals [SD §2.6]'s worked scenario uses to show the shape working. They are reproduced so the scenario can be read, and they are kept in a separate field from 'codes' so that nothing can mistake them for published members. The loader refuses to merge them. They carry the same per-code fields as a published member because one reader validates both — an illustration with a different shape from the thing it illustrates would illustrate nothing.

roleClasses.citation: [SD §2.6] — and this one matters: the scenario attributes a shortfall to 'unknown' rather than omitting attribution, which is the discipline attribution.partyOptional describes

supersededBy.CONSIGNEE_ABSENT: PARTY_ABSENT — [SD §2.4] rule 6 forbids baking the role into the code.
supersededBy.REFUSED_DAMAGE: GOODS_DAMAGED — rule 1: the outcome is encoded in a verb. The outcome axis carries whether the damaged goods were accepted (COMPLETED_WITH_EXCEPTION) or refused (NOT_COMPLETED), which is src:shippeo's LIV/RCA vs REN/AVA and the rule's own worked proof.
supersededBy.SHORT: GOODS_MISSING — the same reason under a name that does not read as a magnitude.

invariants.statement: outcome is legal only where basis = ACTUAL. A plan cannot carry an outcome.
invariants.heldBy: the type system — ActValue<B> in src/assertions.ts admits outcome only at B = 'ACTUAL'
invariants.citation: [SD §2.3] invariant 1 — OTM's rule adopted verbatim (result only on actual/realized)

invariants.statement: reasons[] has at least one member unless outcome = COMPLETED, where it is FORBIDDEN.
invariants.heldBy: the type system — ActOutcome in src/outcomes.ts is a two-member union, so COMPLETED cannot carry reasons and nothing else can omit them

invariants.statement: One act, one outcome, one occurrence time. Where one visit produced two outcomes over two subsets of the goods, it is ONE act with PARTIALLY_COMPLETED and the shortfall named by a Portion in reasons[].appliesTo. Sibling acts on Portions are the required form only when the acts happened at different stops or different times.
invariants.heldBy: prose — a predicate cannot see two records at once; this is a catalog-level rule
